findings.title: R restarts the whole job without asking, even mid-bench, in 3 of 5 station rooms (R is a bench verb in the other 2)
findings.room: all (arcade, arcade-rush, garage, spectrum, cable floors; QFN and observatory bind R differently)
findings.problem: I sat at the arcade bench and pressed R. The page reloaded right away and the job went back to 0:00: tray back in the storeroom, bench progress gone, no confirmation (`progression-24` before, `progression-25` after; arcade-flow.mjs printed `page survived R at bench? false`, `time 0`). Here is why. At the bench, `Game` hands each key to `station.key()` (src/game.ts:164). When the station doesn't bind that key, the key falls through to the walking handler, where `KeyR` and `playing` call `action('restart')`, which runs `location.reload()` (src/game.ts:166, :178). The arcade (src/stations/arcade/station.ts:351-354), garage (src/stations/garage/station.ts:329-332) and spectrum (src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:364-367) benches don't bind R, so R wipes the run. QFN binds R to rotate (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:27), and the observatory binds it to route the cable (src/stations/observatory/station.ts:306). A player who learns 'R = rotate/route' at those benches and then presses R at the arcade or garage bench loses up to 10 minutes of work. On every bench R sits inside the cluster of active keys (E stand up, F flip, D slot, P power, S slot). On cable floors R also restarts at any moment with one keystroke, for example while dragging a 23 m cable in the Meeting. This is the costliest misfire in the game, and it breaks the promise of one key, one verb across rooms.
findings.fix: (1) At the bench, swallow every key the station doesn't use: in src/game.ts:164, after `if(this.station!.key(e.code))…`, add `if(e.code!=='Escape'&&e.code!=='Tab'){e.preventDefault();return;}` so nothing falls through to walking actions. (2) Make restart from play a hold, not a tap: hold R for 0.8 s while a ring fills around the R key on the pause tile, or only allow restart from the pause menu and the result/fail cards. Implement it in src/game.ts:166 with a keydown/keyup timer, and draw the ring in src/ui/game-ui.ts. (3) Reserve R for restart everywhere: remap QFN rotate to T or the wheel, and observatory route to C. Update the prompts in src/stations/qfn/station.ts and src/stations/observatory/station.ts.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/progression/arcade-flow.mjs and expect `page survived R at bench? true` with atBench still true. Add a Playwright case to tests/station-arcade.spec.ts: at the bench press R, then `expect(snapshot.station.trayReady).toBe(true)` and the time is above 0. Do the same for garage and spectrum.
findings.verify_reason: Code: src/game.ts:164 only returns early when station.key() returns true. Otherwise the key falls through to :166, where `KeyR&&playing` calls action('restart'), and that runs location.reload() at :178. The arcade (:351-354), garage (:329-332) and spectrum (:364) maps have no KeyR; QFN (:27) and observatory (:306) bind KeyR. I reproduced it myself in a station the reviewer did not test: seated at the garage bench at t=6.6 s with the robot on the stand, I pressed R. The page reloaded ('survived R at bench? false'), and the run came back at time 0, not at the bench, with the robot back on its pad (verify-progression-02). It is costly and there is no confirmation, but it does not block play, so P1 is right.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-progression/r-keys.mjs (garage: 'page survived R at bench? false', 'after R atBench false time 0')
mockups/review5/shots/progression-24-arcade-bench.jpg and progression-25-arcade-after-R-at-bench.jpg (looked at: 0:05 at bench, then 0:00 back at spawn with the tray objective)

findings.title: The 'R' retry hint on the result card and the Lunch fail card does nothing
findings.problem: The result card's restart button carries an R key badge (src/ui/screens.ts:198), and the Lunch fail card's big button reads 'Retry R' (src/ui/screens.ts:225). Pressing R on either card does nothing. I pressed R on the Playground result card: the page didn't reload and won/screen stayed `result` (playground-win.mjs output, `progression-13`). I pressed R on the Lunch spoil card: `survived R on fail card (no reload)? true`; Enter did reload (lunch-fail.mjs). The cause: GameUI.key only *flags* autostart on R (src/ui/game-ui.ts:119), while the game's own R handler needs `playing=this.running&&!this.won` (src/game.ts:166). Both the win and the Lunch fail set `won=true` (src/lunch-runtime.ts:285). So the one failure the game has (Lunch's spoil and burn) shows a key prompt that lies, exactly when the player wants a quick retry. DR-20 wants under 3 s and no menu from fail to retry. DR-19 says a key never fails to do what its prompt says.
findings.fix: In src/ui/game-ui.ts `key()`, add: `else if((s==='result'||s==='fail')&&e.code==='KeyR'){e.preventDefault();this.restart();}`. restart() already flags autostart and reloads. Keep the Enter branch as it is.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/progression/lunch-fail.mjs and expect `survived R on fail card` to be false and the next snapshot to have time≈0 and running true. Add the same check to tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts (spoil, then R, then data-ready with time 0) and to tests/routes.spec.ts (Playground result, then R).
findings.verify_reason: src/ui/game-ui.ts:119 only calls flagAutostart on R; it never reloads. The game's handler at src/game.ts:166 requires `running&&!won`, and the Lunch fail sets g.won=true at src/lunch-runtime.ts:285. Both cards draw an R badge: the result card at src/ui/screens.ts:198 and the Lunch 'Retry R' button at :225 (visible in progression-40). I reproduced it on the Playground result card: after R, 'survived R on result? true' and the screen stayed on result (verify-progression-04, which still shows the R badge on the retry button). One side effect: R leaves a stale autostart flag in sessionStorage.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-progression/r-keys.mjs ('pg survived R on result? true screen result')

findings.title: Nearly every run grades A overall, so medals, the 'A on three jobs' bonus and replays mean little
findings.problem: Every run I finished in this review graded **A** overall. Playground: 0:05, 0 damage, 0 cost, triple A (`progression-12`). Meeting: 0:21 with 2 breaks, triple A (`progression-36`). Arcade: 0:31 after throwing props, A/A/B, overall A (`progression-29`). Garage, after knocking a chair: A/A/D, overall A (`progression-38`). The causes: overall is the best of three (src/sim/grade.ts:5), cable floors use the 120 s / 10 / 300 default (src/sim/grade.ts:3), and station time limits are 360–720 s (arcade 480, src/stations/arcade/station.ts:81; garage 420, garage/station.ts:77; QFN 720, qfn/station.ts:51; observatory 360; spectrum 540). The time axis alone hands out an A almost every time, so the grade carries no information. The lobby bonus 'Earn an A on three jobs' (src/hub/lobby.ts:46) falls out of the first three jobs automatically. The door medal and the Jobs-board shelf will be a wall of identical gold A's. Good Job's loop is 'replay for a cleaner or faster run' (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md core loop), and that loop needs a grade that moves. Here a sloppy run and a perfect run get the same stamp. Best of three is a hard rule and isn't contested here; the problem is the tuning and what is shown.
findings.fix: (1) Give every level its own `limits` set from a measured par. Run 3–5 human clean runs and set time A at about 1.2× the median human time: for example Playground 40 s, Meeting 150 s, Lunch 300 s, and stations at about 1.3× their median human bench time, not 6–12 min. Pass them through `Level.limits` in src/levels/*.ts and use them at src/game.ts:354 for cable floors too. (2) Keep the overall grade as best of three, per AGENTS 6, but add a mastery mark that replays can chase: 'Crew Gold' = A on all three axes plus all 3 bonus stars, stored per job. Show it as a gold rim on the door medal (src/hub/lobby.ts:94) and on the Jobs-board shelf (src/ui/screens.ts:126). (3) Change the lobby bonus to 'Crew Gold on three jobs'.
findings.verify: A unit test in src/sim/grade.test.ts per level: the scripted clean-route time from tests/*.spec.ts grades A on time, and 3× that time grades C. Rerun progression-38: the garage card still says A overall but shows no Crew Gold rim. Take a lobby shot with mixed results and check the medals differ.
findings.verify_reason: src/sim/grade.ts:3-6: overall = best of the three parts, with a default of 120 s / 10 / 300. The station limits are arcade 480 s (:81), garage 420 s (:77), observatory 360 s (:63), qfn 720 s (:51) and spectrum 540 s (:60). Damage is also an easy A: a floor allows 10 breaks, so any run with 10 or fewer breaks grades A overall no matter its time or cost, and in stations the time axis alone gives an A. Every result card I looked at is overall A: Playground 0:05 A/A/A (verify-progression-04), Arcade A/A/B (progression-29), Garage A/A/D (progression-38). This breaks DR-07 ('Standing still or pure wrecking can't earn A on all three' and per-room tuning), and in practice the overall grade carries no information. The lobby bonus at src/hub/lobby.ts:46 does fall out of any three clears.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/RULES.md:79-85 (DR-07 requires per-room limits; Lunch's use of the default is listed as Known)

findings.title: In station rooms, room chaos is graded on the bench's tiny mistake and parts-credit scales: one knocked chair gives Cost D
findings.room: arcade, arcade-rush, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum
findings.problem: A knocked prop adds `damage++` and its prefab cost (src/game.ts:335), at room scale: chair 25, plant 15, monitor 130 (src/props/prefabs.ts:10-26). In station rooms, win() then adds the bench mistakes and parts credits to the same tallies (src/game.ts:353) and grades them all against the station's limits. Those limits are damage 1–2 mistakes and a cost equal to the parts budget × 1.25, a few credits: garage `cost:…*1.25*10/10` (src/stations/garage/station.ts:77), arcade `limits.cost=ceil(parts*1.25)` (arcade/station.ts:107). Measured: in the garage I knocked one chair before working the bench (0 bench mistakes, elegant parts on all three jobs), and the card shows **28 / D** for cost (`progression-38`, garage-chaos.mjs: `dmg 1 cost 27.8`). In the arcade one broken mug moved cost to B (15 vs a limit of about 13, `progression-29`). Room damage and failed bench tests also share the damage axis with a limit of 1–2, so two knocked mugs score the same as two blown fuses. The station rooms were filled with 80–150 clutter props to make them feel like Good Job floors, yet touching them is punished far harder than on the cable floors (limit 10/300). The message to the player is 'don't play with the room', the opposite of AGENTS 5. The card also mixes units: '28' coins is a chair's repair price added to 2.8 credits of diodes.
findings.fix: Keep room chaos and bench quality on separate scales. In src/game.ts:353-354, grade stations as: damage = room breaks + bench mistakes, against `limits.damage + 10` (a room allowance as on the floors); cost = room cost + bench credits × 10 (show bench credits as coins), against `limits.cost*10 + 300`. A cleaner option: show the bench quality only through the tier stars (the bonuses already cover mistakes and elegance), and let the three Good Job axes stay room-level, with time, breaks and repair cost tuned like the floors. Either way, document the units in src/stations/types.ts.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/progression/garage-chaos.mjs. After one knocked chair and an elegant bench run, the cost row grades A or B, not D, and a blown fuse still costs the 'No failed test' star.
findings.verify_reason: The mechanics are real. src/game.ts:335 adds the prefab cost (chair 25, src/props/prefabs.ts:11) at room scale. win() then adds the bench score (:353) and grades against the station limits (:354). The garage cost limit is about parts×1.25 (station.ts:77), a few credits, so one knocked chair gives Cost 28 = D (progression-38, which I looked at). Arcade showed cost 15 = B after one break (progression-29). The units are mixed on one card. I lowered it to P2 because the overall stamp is best of three: in both cited cases it stayed A, so chaos never costs the job grade. It is a confusing and discouraging row, not a punishment of the overall result. Its weight also overlaps with finding 2 (tuning).
findings.fix_correction: Prefer the reviewer's 'cleaner option': grade the three Good Job axes at room scale (room time, breaks and repair coins, with a per-room `limits`), and express bench quality only through the existing tier and mistake bonus stars. The first option (damage limit = limits.damage+10) would make blown fuses almost free on the damage axis. If it is used, keep bench mistakes as a separate star rather than diluting them.

findings.title: The cable, the game's star, disappears after job 02: 5 of 8 jobs (6 of 9 doors) have no cable act, and their room step is a 2–6 s fetch
findings.room: arcade, arcade-rush, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum
findings.problem: Taken across the whole campaign, the game changes genre halfway. The first three doors are Good Job floors: a springy cable, strain, slingshot, and 24 coworkers reacting (`progression-34` Meeting mid-drag). From door 03 on, the rope is hidden and not simulated: `if(this.station||this.hub)…visible=false` (src/game.ts:92), with no simulateCable/drawCable for stations (src/game.ts:104, :348). Every station level has `obstacles:[]` (src/levels/arcade.ts:26, garage.ts:28, qfn.ts:22, observatory.ts:22, spectrum.ts:32). The room part of each station is one carry: Pip had the arcade tray and was seated at the bench by 5.7 s (arcade-flow.mjs: `held blocks t 2.2`, `atBench true t 5.7`). The rest is a tabletop of 9–13 hotkeys and a side panel (`progression-24`; `garage-play-13-bench-view`; `observatory-play-11-bench-view`). The station jobs are good puzzles, but they read as a second game bolted on. The verbs taught in 00–02 (drag, wrap, plug, slingshot) are never used again, the strain meter never appears again, and the slingshot reward the Playground trains (the pins) has no follow-up. The research doc and R4A already flagged that the cable is missing in stations. Seen as one progression, it is the main reason the campaign stops feeling like Circuit Crew after about 3 jobs.
findings.fix:
Give every station one real room cable act that feeds the bench, using the existing rope sim. Allow `station` levels to set `length>0` and keep the cable when they do (src/game.ts:92/104/348 checks become `this.station&&!this.level.length`). Per room, with a reel anchor and obstacles in src/levels/<id>.ts:
- Arcade: the bench is dead until Pip drags the bench's mains lead (14 m) from the wall socket across the busy hall. After each fix, the cabinet's own plug must be plugged back in, so fling-able beanbags and cones are on the route.
- Garage: route the robot's charge lead from the pad to the test stand around the lifts.
- Observatory: the noisy motor cable is the cable the player reroutes. The bench already has 'ROUTE: PAST MOTOR', so make it a physical drag.
- QFN: carry the finished board on a reel cart to the reflow oven.
- Spectrum: the pod's feed cable limits how far the pod can go.
Add one chaos shortcut per room: an overstretched slingshot that knocks the storeroom shelf down and spills the tray onto the bench.
findings.verify: `snap().rope.maxLength>0` and the cable is visible in the start shot of every station level (DR-05 check). Add one spec per station that reaches `won` using a cable act, plus a slingshot spec that moves a prop more than 1 m.
findings.verify_reason: src/game.ts:92 hides the plug, target, socket and anchor when station||hub. :104 runs simulateCable and drawCable only for non-station levels, and :348 skips the cable sim for stations. Every station level has obstacles:[] (arcade.ts:26, garage.ts:28, qfn.ts:22, observatory.ts:22, spectrum.ts:32). My runs reached the bench at 6.6 s in the garage and 6.7 s in the arcade, so the room part is a few seconds of carrying. This is the open R4A issue (mockups/review4/DESIGN_A.md:7, :218), still unfixed rather than a regression. It breaks DR-05 'in every playable room'.
extra_evidence: mockups/review4/DESIGN_A.md:7 and :218 (same finding in R4, still open)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-progression-02-garage-after-R.jpg (no cable or reel visible in the garage)
findings.fix_correction: The proposed gate `this.station&&!this.level.length` does not work: every station level already sets `length:10` (arcade.ts:26, garage.ts:28, qfn.ts:22, observatory.ts:22, spectrum.ts:32), so that check would turn the rope on in all stations at once with a meaningless anchor at (-10,6). Add an explicit Level flag (for example `cable:true`, or a `stationCable:{anchor,length,target}` block) and gate src/game.ts:92/:104/:348 on it. Set real anchors, lengths and obstacles per room as each cable act is built.

findings.title: Station jobs share one template (carry, 'Sit at the bench (E)' step, button sub-jobs), and none has a chaos route or chaos bonus
findings.problem:
All five station jobs follow the same script:
1. Carry one thing (tray, robot, parts crate, motor cart, pod).
2. Complete a separate objective step whose only content is pressing E: 'Step up to the service bench (E)' (src/stations/arcade/station.ts:110), 'Sit at the garage bench (E)' (garage/station.ts:98), 'Sit at the layout bench (E)' (qfn/station.ts:72), 'Sit at the signal bench (E)' (observatory/station.ts:86), 'Sit at the dispatch desk (E)' (spectrum/station.ts:87).
3. Solve 3–5 sub-jobs by picking parts with number keys and slotting them with letter keys.
4. Get the result card.

Only the spectrum job sends Pip back into the room between sub-jobs (pod and mirrors, spectrum/station.ts:89-92), and only the garage has a payoff in the room afterwards (the robot drives its route). Every station bonus list is bench precision only: 'reliable', 'elegant', 'no failed test/fuse' (arcade :119-121, garage :103-104, qfn :75-77, observatory :89-91, spectrum :95-97). None is physical or chaos, unlike the Playground pins (src/ui/objectives.ts:28). So for a chaos player, 5 of the 8 jobs offer nothing to chase in the room, and the dense clutter is scenery that costs points (see the grading finding). Played in order, 03→07 feel like the same room five times with a different panel.
findings.fix:
(1) Delete the 'Sit at the bench (E)' step from all five stations; the marker and the 'E Work at the bench' prompt already cover it. (2) Give each station one physical or chaos bonus with a target that is visible in the survey:
- Arcade: 'Knock the prize pyramid over with a thrown beanbag'.
- Garage: 'Ride the robot's route without touching it'.
- QFN: 'Stack the scrap boards'.
- Observatory: 'Roll the motor cart into the far wall'.
- Spectrum: 'Bounce the beam off three mirrors'.

Put these in each station's `bonuses` array. (3) Vary the room beat between sub-jobs, as spectrum does. For example, the arcade kid carries the fixed cabinet's plug away and Pip must re-seat it, and the garage robot needs a push back onto the stand after each test.
findings.verify: Each station's `job.bonuses` contains at least one bonus whose `ok()` reads room physics (prop positions or velocities). A scripted chaos spec earns it. The survey shot shows its target.
findings.verify_reason: I checked every cited line. Each station has a step whose whole content is pressing E: arcade :110, garage :98, qfn :72, observatory :86, spectrum :87. Every bonus list is bench-precision only: arcade :114-121, garage :101-104, qfn :74-77, observatory :88-91, spectrum :94-97. The Playground has the in-world pins bonus (src/ui/objectives.ts:28). Only spectrum sends Pip back into the room between sub-jobs (:89-92). This breaks DR-10, which says every room has a chaos bonus that can be found in the world.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/progression-29-arcade-result.jpg and progression-38-garage-result-after-chaos.jpg (bonus lists are all bench precision)

findings.title: The difficulty and concept curve spikes at job 02 (Lunch), then resets to new domains with no reuse
findings.problem: Job order (src/levels/index.ts:10): 00 Playground (cable feel, 3 steps, about 5 s scripted), 01 Meeting (route plus load budget, 3 steps, 21 s scripted), then 02 Lunch. Lunch has 7 steps (src/ui/objectives.ts:40-50) and the only two fail states in the game. Simply exploring for 120 s with the fridge unpowered ends the job: lunch-fail.mjs spoiled at exactly t=120 with no input (`progression-40`). Its HUD has 4 widgets at once (bake, belt and lift chain, fridge bar, two breaker gauges, `progression-39`), and it introduces budgets per breaker, splitters adding up, cable rating and heat, start-up kick, capacitor, water short and the fridge as storage together. Then 03 Arcade drops back to Ohm's law for an LED, a more basic idea than Lunch's start-up kick. 04 Garage (flyback diode, TVS, star ground), 05 QFN (PCB routing), 06 Observatory (filters, S/N) and 07 Spectrum (EM bands through materials) each open a new domain and reuse nothing from the job before. Spectrum isn't about circuits at all. The designer's own time budgets show the uneven length: floors 120 s by default, stations 360–720 s. In Turing Tumble terms, each job should add one idea and reuse the last one; here Lunch adds about 7, and the stations don't build on each other.
evidence: docs/GAME_DESIGN.md (Design process rules: one new idea per level)
findings.fix:
Reorder `levels` in src/levels/index.ts, and renumber Level.number/LOOK, the lobby slots and the `next` links, into a chain where each job reuses the previous idea:
1. 00 Playground: a loop needs a switch.
2. 01 Meeting: length and route, plus loads add up on a strip.
3. 02 Arcade: current is set by resistance.
4. 03 Lunch: budgets per breaker, plus the start-up kick and the capacitor. Arcade's current makes the 'bars' meaningful.
5. 04 Garage: inductive kick. It reuses the kick and the capacitor from Lunch.
6. 05 Observatory: noise and filters (reuses the capacitor and coil).
7. 06 QFN: layout, decoupling and the loop (reuses decoupling and the shared return).
8. 07 Spectrum: waves, as the finale.

Also make Lunch's spoil timer start only once the player first enters the kitchen or touches a cable (src/sim/lunch.ts). Otherwise a first-time explorer fails for looking around.
findings.verify: Write a table of the new and reused idea per job in docs/GAME_DESIGN.md. Rerun lunch-fail.mjs with no input: no spoil card at t=120 until the kitchen has been entered. Run tests/lobby.spec.ts with the new door order.
findings.verify_reason: The order is in src/levels/index.ts:11, and Lunch has 7 steps (src/ui/objectives.ts:40-50). The fridge math in src/sim/lunch.ts:5-9 starts at temperature .28 and warms .006/s unpowered, so it fails at exactly (1-.28)/.006 = 120 s with no input. That matches lunch-fail.mjs and the fail card in progression-40, which I looked at. Lunch is the only room that can fail: spoil, plus burn at :12. The claim that later jobs reuse little is a design judgment, but it is consistent with each station's unrelated concept and with DR-27 (one new idea that reuses the previous one). A first-time explorer failing at 2:00 for looking around also brushes against AGENTS 5's spirit.
extra_evidence: src/sim/lunch.ts:8 (+.006/s unpowered; failed at 1.0 means 120 s)
src/sim/lunch.test.ts:5 (the test confirms spoilage with no power)
findings.fix_correction: The reorder is a heavy change (Level.number, LOOK, lobby slots, next links, tests and thumbnails). Do the cheap part first, since it fixes the worst player-facing symptom: start the fridge warming only after the player first enters the kitchen or picks up a cable end, or lower the start temperature or warm rate so an idle player gets about 4 minutes. Then plan the reorder as a separate change, with the reuse table in docs/GAME_DESIGN.md.

findings.title: The Arcade Rush lock leaks: the Jobs board and the URL bypass it, any grade (even C) unlocks it, and the lobby then sends players to Rush as 'next'
findings.problem: `requires` is only checked by the lobby door (src/hub/lobby.ts:73, :121, :132). On a fresh profile, the title's Jobs board lists 03R Arcade Rush as playable, and Play launches it (`progression-17`: the Play button aria-label is 'Play 03R Arcade Rush' with no progress at all). playSelected/the data-job click (src/ui/game-ui.ts:77, :99) never check it, and `?level=arcade-rush` also loads straight in. Where the lock does apply, it opens on any result: with Arcade seeded at grade C, the Rush door opened and the lobby's job card and bouncing marker named '03R · Arcade Rush' as the next job, ahead of 04 Garage (`progression-19`, `progression-21`). The cause is that `nextUnfinished` and the lobby steps walk `levels` in order, and Rush is a required step there (src/hub/lobby.ts:41-43). The intent is 'unlocked once the station is understood' (docs/EXPANSION_PLAN.md audit table). In practice a player who scraped a C is pushed into a timed version of the job they just struggled with, before the next new job. 'Finish every job' (src/hub/lobby.ts:45) also requires Rush, so the optional mode is mandatory for the hub's bonus.
findings.fix: (1) Add `export const isLocked=(l:Level)=>!!l.requires&&!(bestFor(l.requires)&&bestFor(l.requires)!.grade<='B')` to src/ui/store.ts, which unlocks at B or better. Use it in lobby.ts:73, in jobTag (src/ui/screens.ts:109, with a padlock overlay and a disabled Play), in GameUI.playSelected, and in main.ts boot, which redirects a locked `?level=` to the lobby. (2) Leave Rush out of the hub's required steps and out of 'Finish every job'. Add `optional:true` to Level, filter it in src/hub/lobby.ts:41 and :45, and in `nextUnfinished` (store.ts:19). Offer Rush as a bonus instead: 'Beat a Rush shift with 8 cabinets'.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/progression/lobby-progress.mjs. On a fresh profile the Jobs board shows Rush with a padlock and Play does nothing. With Arcade at C, the Rush door stays locked and the marker points at 04 Garage. Add a case to tests/lobby.spec.ts: `page.goto('/?level=arcade-rush')` on a fresh profile lands in the lobby.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced all three leaks. (a) On a fresh profile (localStorage cleared), the Jobs board selects 03R and Go's aria-label reads 'Play 03R Arcade Rush'. Clicking it navigated to ?level=arcade-rush, which loaded and ran with the Rush timer at 2:56 (verify-progression-06). (b) A direct URL loads, since `requires` is only read at src/hub/lobby.ts:73 and :132; there is no check in game-ui.ts:77/:99 or in boot. (c) I seeded Arcade at C with 00–03 done. The lobby doors showed arcade-rush with locked=false, and the job card named '03R · Arcade Rush' as the next step, ahead of 04 Garage (verify-progression-07). 'Finish every job' (lobby.ts:45) iterates all levels, Rush included.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-progression/rush-lock.mjs ('go label Play 03R Arcade Rush'; 'url ...?level=arcade-rush screen play'; 'rush? true'; doors arcade-rush [false,false]; 'lobby card 03R · Arcade Rush')

findings.title: Bonus stars aren't saved and the result card never shows the previous best, so there is no hook to replay
findings.problem: Each job has three bonus goals, shown as three stars on the job card and as a ★ list on the result card (src/ui/game-ui.ts:216-217). The save record only keeps `{grade,time,damage,cost}` (src/ui/store.ts:4, :13). Stars earned are thrown away when the card closes, so the lobby door, the door medal and the Jobs-board tag can't show how many stars a job has. After finishing Playground and returning, the door looks the same as one finished with zero stars (`progression-14`, `progression-20`). The result card shows this run's numbers only, with no previous best and no delta. The 'new best' star appears only when the overall grade improves (`improved:!old||run.grade<old.grade`, store.ts:15), and since almost every run is A (see the grading finding), it shows on the first clear and never again, even when a replay cuts time from 0:21 to 0:12. `record` also takes the best of each stat separately (store.ts:13), so the Jobs-board 'best' row can combine a time from one run with damage from another, a run that never happened. Taken together, a finished job offers no visible reason to go back in.
findings.fix: (1) Extend `Best` with `stars:number` (a bitmask of the three bonuses, OR-merged across runs), and pass `this.objectives.results()` into record() at src/ui/game-ui.ts:208. (2) Show stars on the door plate under the medal (src/hub/lobby.ts:94: three small star plates), on the job tag (src/ui/screens.ts:115) and in the lobby (a hub bonus 'Collect 15 stars'). (3) On the result card, under each row, print the previous best and a green or red delta ('best 0:21 · −0:09'). Fire the newbest star and bell when any stat or star improves, not only the grade.
findings.verify: Seed a run with 1 star, replay with 2, and confirm localStorage holds `stars:3` (bitwise OR). In the lobby the Playground door shows 2 of 3 stars lit. Retake progression-12: a delta line appears under the time row on a second clear.
findings.verify_reason: src/ui/store.ts:4 Best holds only {grade,time,damage,cost}. src/ui/game-ui.ts:208 passes no bonus results to record(), and the stars are only rendered at :216-217. improved = grade-only (store.ts:15). After the Playground clear, localStorage held only {grade,time,damage,cost} (r-keys.mjs output: '{"playground":{"grade":"A","time":5.08,"damage":0,"cost":0}}'), even though the card showed 2 of 3 stars. One correction to the framing: keeping each stat's best separately is deliberate (the comment at store.ts:3 says 'Each stat keeps its own best'). That is a documented choice, not a bug, but the 'composite run' point stands as a UX observation.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-progression-03-pg-result.jpg (2 of 3 stars lit on the card)

findings.title: The lobby barely celebrates or signposts progress: the wing lamp sits at the frame edge, medals are about 10 px, Pip returns to the centre
findings.problem: After finishing Playground and choosing Jobs, Pip reloads into the lobby at the fixed spawn (0, 5.5) (src/game.ts:81 uses `level.spawn`), not at the door he came out of. Nothing happens: no wing light-up, no cheer from the 3 coworkers, no camera beat. The reward is a lamp at y 3.35 above the door (src/hub/lobby.ts:96). At the lobby game camera it lands on the very top edge of the frame as a faint glow dot (`progression-14`; `progression-30`, the arcade door at the top border). The medal is a 0.34 m plate (src/hub/lobby.ts:94), about 10 px at the default camera, and only readable at zoom 9 (`progression-20`). The 'next job' marker is a small cone over the door at the back wall (`progression-02`, at about (340, 60) px) and is easy to miss. Doors show only a number and name; nothing tells a new player what kind of job is behind 05 versus 06. The portal thumbnail only shows once the door opens. The lobby is the only place that communicates the campaign, and today it reads like a corridor of identical doors.
findings.fix: (1) On a return via jobs-reload, pass `&from=<id>` in GameUI.toJobs (src/ui/game-ui.ts:76) and spawn Pip at that door's `at` facing the atrium. If the job was newly finished, play a 1.5 s beat: the door lamp flicks on with a spark burst, the coworkers cheer, and the camera does a short push on the door. (2) Move the lamp down to y 2.95 and put a lit colour band across the frame head (src/hub/lobby.ts:96). Double the medal plate to 0.6 m and place it on the leaf at eye height. (3) Make the next-job marker 2× bigger and add a lit floor arrow decal in the door's colour leading from the reception ring. (4) Put one wordless pictogram per door on the leaf panel (lamp, projector, tray, LED, robot, chip, dish, waves), reusing `Level.badge` icons as a decal.
findings.verify: Retake progression-14 after a fresh Playground clear: Pip stands at the Playground door, its lamp is lit inside the frame (not touching the top edge), and the medal is at least 24 px tall at the game camera.
findings.verify_reason: src/game.ts:81 always spawns at level.spawn. The lamp is at y 3.35 (src/hub/lobby.ts:96) and the medal plate is 0.34 m (:94). In my lobby shot with progress (verify-progression-07) the wing lamps sit on the top border of the frame and the grade plates beside the doors are tiny letters, readable only by zooming in. The job card works, but the reward is barely readable. Polish, so P2.

findings.title: Workshop practice offers no reason to use it: it's identical to normal play, only covers stations, and the picker leaks input
findings.problem: The picker lists only the 5 station jobs (`levels.filter(l=>l.station&&!l.id.endsWith('-rush'))`, src/hub/lobby.ts:112), so the three cable floors, where the cable feel is learned, can't be practised. A practice run is the normal run with `record()` skipped (src/ui/game-ui.ts:208). Every rule, timer, mistake and grade is identical; there are no free parts, unlimited fuses or hints. Since `record()` already keeps only the best (src/ui/store.ts:13), a normal run can never hurt your record either, so a practice run has no advantage. The picker text says 'nothing is graded or recorded' (src/hub/lobby.ts:113), but the practice result card still stamps a grade. EXPANSION_PLAN describes the Workshop as 'try parts, no penalties'. As for the picker itself, which re-checks L3: the job card and the 'E Workshop: practise any station' prompt pill stay live behind the modal (`progression-09`), and holding W moved Pip from (7.5, 5.5) to (7.0, 4.2) while the picker was open (lobby.mjs output). Spelling: 'practise any station' on the arch and the picker versus 'Practice · not recorded' on the card (verb and noun are fine in British usage, but the page mixes them).
evidence: docs/EXPANSION_PLAN.md (audit: Free Workshop mode, try parts, no penalties)
findings.verify: Rerun lobby.mjs: `player after W w/ picker` is unchanged, and the shot shows no prompt pill behind the modal. Add a practice spec: in an arcade practice run, power cabinet 1 with the block across the LED, and `snap().station.mistakes` stays 0.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches. The picker list is stations only (src/hub/lobby.ts:112). Practice only skips record() (game-ui.ts:208) and still stamps a grade (:214). The picker's only key listener is a capture-phase Escape (lobby.ts:115), so the game's keydown handler (game.ts:163-166) still adds movement keys. The reviewer's movement evidence was invalid: lobby.mjs used `g.advance(.5,['KeyW'])`, which injects keys straight into the driver (src/game.ts:465) and moves Pip regardless of the UI. I re-tested in real time without ?manual: with the picker open, holding W for 0.9 s moved Pip from (7.29, 4.76) to (7.00, 4.25). The 'E Workshop: practise any station' pill stays visible behind the modal (verify-progression-10).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-progression/picker-realtime.mjs ('before W {x:7.29,z:4.76} after W {x:7.00,z:4.25} picker still true')
src/game.ts:465 (driver advance overrides keys, so lobby.mjs's evidence does not prove the leak)
findings.fix_correction: Put the picker guard at the very top of the keydown listener, before `this.keys.add(e.code)` (src/game.ts:163), not at :166. Also clear `game.keys` when the picker opens. Otherwise a key already held when E is pressed keeps Pip walking.

findings.title: Two of the three lobby bonuses are the same check, and the third is automatic
findings.problem: Lobby bonuses (src/hub/lobby.ts:44-47): 'Finish every job' is `jobs.every(l=>!!bestFor(l.id))`, and 'Light every wing' is `this.doors.every(d=>d.done)`, where `done=!!bestFor(level.id)` (lobby.ts:73). They are the same condition, so the hub's star row always lights its 1st and 3rd stars together. 'Earn an A on three jobs' is satisfied by almost any three clears (see the grading finding). The hub's job card therefore offers no real meta goal across the campaign, and 'Finish every job' also requires the optional Arcade Rush.
findings.fix: Replace them with distinct, chaseable meta goals: 'Collect 15 bonus stars' (needs stars persisted), 'Crew Gold on three jobs' (A on all axes), and 'Beat a Rush shift with 8+ cabinets'. Keep 'Finish every job' as the main step-dot progress, not as a bonus.
findings.verify: Unit-test the lobby bonuses with a seeded store: finishing every job lights exactly one of the three stars.
findings.verify_reason: src/hub/lobby.ts:45 checks `jobs.every(l=>!!bestFor(l.id))`. :47 checks `this.doors.every(d=>d.done)`, with done=!!bestFor(level.id) (:73). The snapshot lists 9 doors for the 9 levels (rush-lock.mjs output), so the two conditions are identical. :46 is near-automatic given finding 2.

findings.title: The 'next job' chain stops after 03: station results switch from 'Next' to 'Jobs', so the flow changes mid-campaign
findings.problem: Only the cable floors set `next` (playground→meeting, meeting→lunch, lunch→arcade: src/levels/playground.ts:2, meeting.ts:33, lunch.ts:15). Arcade, garage, qfn, observatory and spectrum have none, and arcadeRush sets `next:undefined` (arcade.ts:31). So the primary button on the result card is a big yellow '→ 01' on the first three jobs (`progression-12`, `progression-36`). From the Arcade on it turns into 'Jobs' (`progression-29`, `progression-38`; src/ui/screens.ts:182-183). Players who learned 'Enter = next job' are suddenly sent back to the hub, where the marker recommends Arcade Rush. Either flow is fine, but mixing them makes the campaign's structure unclear (is the hub or the chain the main path?).
findings.fix: Pick one model. Recommended: the primary button always walks back to HQ with the from-door return beat (see the lobby finding), so the hub is the progression screen; keep 'Next job →' as a secondary button computed from `nextUnfinished(levels)`, not `level.next`. If the chain is kept instead, set `next` on every level in the reordered campaign (arcade→garage→…→spectrum) and drop `next` from the last one only.
findings.verify: Clear any level, and the result card offers the same button layout. Rerun progression-29: there is a secondary 'next' showing the next unfinished door number.
findings.verify_reason: Only playground.ts:2, meeting.ts:33 and lunch.ts:15 set next. arcadeRush sets next:undefined (arcade.ts:31) and the other stations set none. screens.ts:182-183 switches the primary button to 'Jobs'. This shows in the result cards: Playground has '→ 01' (verify-progression-04) while Arcade and Garage have 'Jobs' (progression-29, progression-38).

findings.title: Room lengths are very uneven: Playground is solved in 5 s, while the designer's limits range from 120 s (floors) to 720 s (stations)
findings.problem: Scripted clean solves measured in this review: Playground 5.1 s (playground-win.mjs: three walkTo legs and two keys), Meeting 21.4 s (meeting-time2.mjs), Arcade 31.6 s, Garage 26.2 s. Lunch can't meet its 120 s default (DR-07 Known). The per-room time limits that encode the designer's expected length span 120 s (all floors, src/sim/grade.ts:3) to 360–720 s (stations), a 6× spread. GAME_DESIGN's core loop says 5–10 min per level. The Playground tutorial in particular finishes before the player has had to wrap the cable round a pillar, see strain colour or try the slingshot: the clean route is a 15 m L-shaped walk (tests/routes.spec.ts:21-22), and the result card stamps triple A. The cable feel that every later floor relies on is never really exercised in the tutorial.
findings.fix: Make the Playground teach the cable by need. Move the lamp socket behind the second pillar so the 19 m reel only reaches if the cable wraps the right side of a pillar (src/levels/playground.ts target/obstacles). Add a low barrier the cable must be flung over, which makes the slingshot and the pins part of the route. Then set per-level limits from human-timed runs (see the grading finding), and bring the station limits down to about 1.3× median human time, so all jobs fall within about 2× of the median (DR-08).
findings.verify: Re-time all clean specs with `snap().time` at `won` and check the max is within 2× the median. The Playground clean spec must contain at least one rope bend (`snap().rope.bends.length>=1`) before plugging in.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the Playground scripted clean solve at 5.1 s (r-keys.mjs: 'pg won true time 5.1'). The time limits range from 120 s (grade.ts:3) to 720 s (qfn :51). Caveat: these are bot times on an optimal script, and human first-run times will be several times longer. Use DR-08 with human-timed or at least consistently scripted runs, and include Lunch, which cannot finish quickly because of its fixed 20 s bake, 9 s conveyor and 6 s lift (src/sim/lunch.ts:10-14).
extra_evidence: src/sim/lunch.ts:10-14 (fixed bake, belt and lift durations set a floor on Lunch's time)

findings.title: Meeting: walking past the mail cart knocks the second reel off, and the prompt then says 'Grab the cart'
findings.problem: Following the spec's clean coupler route with a 0.1 s settle after each key (meeting-time.mjs), the E at (−3, 5.3) grabbed `mail-cart` instead of `extension`. The rope stayed at 23.2 m, and the drag stalled at x 9.35 with strain 1.02, short of the strip. A probe shows the extension reel had been knocked off the cart to (−1.59, 4.88), about 1.3 m away beside a desk. The prompt read 'E Grab the cart' (`progression-43`). The spec passes on its exact timing (I ran tests/routes.spec.ts -g coupler: 2 passed), so the clean route depends on the reel staying perched on a cart that Pip bumps while fetching the coupler beside it. `nearest()` sorts by reach only (src/game.ts:192), so the heavy cart beats the job reel. For a player, the second reel quietly disappears from the cart and E offers to push the cart.
findings.fix: Give id'd job items priority in `nearest()`: subtract 0.6 m from the reach of any prop whose `spec.id` matches the current step's item, or any id'd item. Seat the extension reel in a tray on the cart (a fixed joint until grabbed) so a bump doesn't spill it. Add the extension to the respawn rule (DR-15) if it lands more than 2 m from home.
findings.verify: Rerun meeting-time.mjs unchanged and expect `held e extension` and maxLen 37.2. Add a spec that shoves the mail cart with Pip, then checks the extension is still on it, or that E still grabs the extension.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it with my own run of the spec route. The extension started on the cart at (-3.0, 4.70). After the coupler fetch and the walk back it was at (-1.27, 5.04), knocked off onto the floor. Standing at (-3.3, 5.3), the prompt read 'E Grab the cart' and E took 'mail-cart' (verify-progression-09). The diagnosis in the finding is wrong, though. reach() already gives id'd items a 2 m priority (src/game.ts:194), but the cart also has an id ('mail-cart', src/levels/meeting.ts:27), so the priority does not separate them. The reel was also outside nearest()'s 1.65 m filter (game.ts:192), so it was not a candidate at all.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-progression/lobby-meeting.mjs ('at cart ext {x:-1.27,z:5.04} cart {x:-2.81,z:4.54}', 'prompt E Grab the cart', 'held e mail-cart')
findings.fix_correction: The proposed 'subtract 0.6 m for id'd items' already exists, as −2 m at src/game.ts:194, and would change nothing. Instead: (1) remove the id from the mail cart or exclude it from the bonus, or prefer the current step's item by id over other id'd props; (2) seat the extension on the cart, for example with a fixed joint or a raised lip until it is first grabbed, so a bump can't spill it; (3) DR-15 respawn covers only y>2.1 (game.ts:342), so it would not catch a reel on the floor. A reel 1.7 m away is still recoverable by walking over, which is why this stays P2.

findings.title: Draw calls in the hub and at the arcade bench are well over budget (663 in a 15-prop lobby, about 1200 at the arcade bench)
findings.problem: `snap().drawCalls` at the lobby start was 663 (lobby.mjs) for a room with 15 props, 9 doors and a board. Every door has a portal mesh, several signPlates, a leaf, a lamp and a glow, and the board has one signPlate per job (src/hub/lobby.ts:61-63, :77-98). At the arcade bench, snapshots during the run show 1160–1207 draw calls (arcade-full.mjs act-fail dumps), matching the open A13 item. FPS held at 60 on this host GPU, but the hub is the screen every session passes through, and weaker machines will feel it first.
findings.fix: Bake each door's static frame and sign plates into one merged mesh per door (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries, as LR15 did for Lunch). Render the directory board's 9 plates into one canvas texture. Merge the arcade bench's static bins and labels the same way.
findings.verify: `snap().drawCalls` is at most 250 at the lobby start and in the arcade bench view.
findings.verify_reason: Measured myself: lobby drawCalls 586 (reviewer reported 663). Arcade start 1497, arcade bench 1184, at 60 fps on the host GPU. DR-24's limit is about 250, and both rooms are well over it.

notes.fun: Moment to moment, the cable floors deliver the Good Job promise. The Meeting mid-drag shot (progression-34) has a springy cable snaking between pillars and 24 coworkers around it, and the win push-ins land with confetti, a cheer and a card that thuds in. The campaign as a whole is weaker. After job 02 the cable, strain meter and slingshot vanish for the remaining 5 jobs (6 doors). Every station follows one template: a 2–6 s carry, an objective step that is just 'press E', then button sub-jobs. No station has a chaos route or a chaos bonus, and room breakage there is graded on bench-sized scales (one chair = Cost D). Every run I finished graded A overall: Playground 5 s, Meeting 21 s, Arcade 31 s with breaks, Garage with a D in cost. Bonus stars aren't saved and the card shows no previous best, so replay motivation rests entirely on curiosity. The Workshop practice mode is the normal run without saving, which normal play already risks nothing, so it has no purpose. What works: fast transitions (door to playable room in about 1.5 s, back to HQ in about 0.5 s), the door spring and the portal peek, the rush countdown card, and the result card's count-up and axis cable.
notes.clarity: The lobby gets the basics right. The job card names the next door ('00 · Cable Playground', moving to '01 · Big Meeting' after a clear), a marker bounces over it, the prompt reads 'E Enter 00 · Cable Playground', and a locked door explains itself ('Locked: finish 03 · Overheating Arcade first'). Signposting of progress is faint: the wing lamp sits on the top edge of the frame, the medals are about 10 px, Pip reloads at the centre rather than the door he left, and nothing happens on return. The doors don't hint at what is behind them. The Rush lock leaks through the Jobs board and the URL, opens on a C, and then the lobby recommends Rush ahead of the next new job. The result flow switches from 'Next →' (00–02) to 'Jobs' (03+). The title still shows the unclear 'HQ' badge on Play and a faint gamepad icon (L4). Text volume in the lobby is low and the card is short, which is good. The R key hints on the result and fail cards are false.
notes.teaching: Taken as a curriculum, the order is the weak point. Playground (cable feel) and Meeting (length plus loads adding up on a breaker) build nicely. Then Lunch, job 02, introduces about 7 ideas at once with the game's only fail states, and a 120 s idle timer can fail a player who is just exploring. Arcade then drops back to Ohm's law, a more basic idea than Lunch's start-up kick. Garage, QFN, Observatory and Spectrum each open a new domain without reusing the previous job's idea. Spectrum isn't a circuit job at all. Suggested chain: Playground → Meeting → Arcade (resistance sets current) → Lunch (budgets, kick, capacitor) → Garage (inductive kick, reusing the kick) → Observatory (filters, reusing C and L) → QFN (decoupling and return) → Spectrum.
notes.playability: No crashes: every script's `g.close()` returned [] (lobby, playground-win, lobby-progress, arcade-flow, arcade-full, meeting-time×2, garage-chaos, lunch-fail, transition, mailcart-probe), and saving to localStorage works and survives reloads (`circuit-crew:best:v1`). Two key problems stand out. First, R wipes the whole job instantly from the arcade, garage and spectrum benches, because unbound bench keys fall through to the walking handler, while QFN and observatory use R as a bench verb. Second, R on the result and fail cards, which display an R hint, does nothing. The Workshop picker lets W move Pip under the modal, and the prompt pill stays live behind it. In the Meeting, Pip easily bumps the second reel off the mail cart, after which E offers 'Grab the cart'. The Meeting clean spec still passes on its exact timing. The lobby uses 663 draw calls and the arcade bench about 1200.
notes.models: Not the focus of this dimension. From the progression angle: lobby doors read well up close (progression-20), with a colour frame, number panel, name plate and medal, but they read as one repeated slab at the game camera. The wing-lamp reward is too high to see, and the medal plate is too small. The Meeting win shot still frames the projector wall and blobs without Pip (progression-36, QA 10 / M3 still open).
